- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.33) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; increase forecast downward by 1–2% to match true decline.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 2–4 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply slight downward bias (−0.5% to −2%) for 3–7 days if price is above 3σ from recent mean.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates true price in early days (1–5) when sentiment is positive; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for first 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model often misjudges direction; apply caution and reduce confidence in 3–5 day forecasts.
- When sentiment is negative and price is near support, model often ignores support; increase forecast downward by 1–2% to align with true support levels.
